t: A low-cost Wi-Fi and Bluetooth chip for smart gadgets, screens and small AI tricks.
steps: Buy an ESP32-S3 board from a maker shop, such as a Feather-size or thumb-sized board.
Get a USB cable that matches the board and carries data.
Install the free Arduino IDE on your computer.
Add the ESP32 board package in the Arduino board manager.
Pick your board and its USB port in the menus.
Upload the Blink example and watch the light.
Try the WiFiScan example to list nearby networks.
meta: Open Board. From $7.49. A few stores.
